original_article: Educational technology, or EdTech, has fundamentally reshaped how knowledge is delivered and consumed around the globe. By integrating digital tools like interactive software, virtual classrooms, and mobile applications into standard curricula, educators can create dynamic learning environments tailored to diverse student needs. Personalized learning algorithms analyze individual student progress in real time, allowing teachers to identify learning gaps early and adapt instruction accordingly. Furthermore, EdTech breaks down geographical barriers, enabling students in remote or underserved regions to access high-quality courses, lectures, and educational resources previously out of reach. However, the rapid expansion of digital learning also highlights significant challenges, most notably the digital divide. Unequal access to high-speed internet and hardware leaves disadvantaged communities at a risk of falling behind. Additionally, reliance on digital platforms raises valid concerns regarding student data privacy, screen time management, and the potential reduction of essential face-to-face social interactions. To maximize the benefits of educational technology, institutions must balance innovative digital solutions with equitable access, strong privacy safeguards, and traditional collaborative teaching practices.
